newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA RAND/BONDS CLOSING REPORT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA RAND/BONDS CLOSING REPORT.

text.p: A late spurt of dollar demand by local importers pulled the rand off its strongest level at the Friday close after it had initially been buoyed by offshore and local exporter dollar selling.
At the local finish, the currency was pegged at 4.6780/6820 against the dollar from 4.6870/6920 at Thursday's finish.
Dealers said the currency was initially boosted by exporter and some offshore dollar selling. That helped the rand firm to a day's strongest level of 4.6660 bid against the greenback.
But it then ran into New York-based dollar buying as well as importer demand which pulled it back up to its closing levels.
"We saw both importers and exporters...New York was a (dollar) buyer and London was on both sides," a trader said.
Dealers said volumes on the day were patchy with few players reluctant to take any sizeable positions ahead of the weekend.
"With it being Friday one got the feeling that people were not prepared to sit on any positions which made it a bit choppy," one said.
Against the crosses, the rand held relatively steady at 7.7966/8082 against sterling from 7.7991/8121 overnight and at at 0.3214/19 marks against 0.3212/16 previously.

Dealers said the rand was expected to remain trapped in a 4.6650 to 4.70 range next week with importers halting any further strength and the Reserve Bank expected to cap any weakness beyong 4.6950 bid.
Bond yields took heart from the steadier rand after initially being encouraged by sturdy government revenue figures, although technical factors came into play late in the day.
The key R150 settled at 16.00 percent after trading in a 15.965 to 16.03 percent range.

Traders said figures showing exchequer issues in the first seven months of 1996/97 were 99.104 billion rand, or 57.1 percent of the year budget and revenue at 84.926 billion rand, or 58.6 percent of the year budget, spurred early buying.
"The exchequer figures helped the market a bit...we saw local institutions buying and jobbers covering their short positions," one dealer said.
However, the market's failure to breach technical resistance at the 15.97 level cut any hopes of further strength short and the market retraced to the 16.00 percent level.
"After we failed to break the jobbers went short again," a dealer said.
A break of the 15.97 percent level could bring the 15.88 to 15.92 percent into target range next week, dealers added.
Foreigners sold a net 61.87 million rand worth of South African bonds on Thursday after selling a net 111.66 million rand on Wednesday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative volumes stood at 21.82 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement day -- from 7.01 billion rand on Wednesday.
Three-month NCD rates were unchanged at between 16.95 and 17.20 percent while the 90-day BA rate was held at 16.30 to 16.75.
The daily money market shortage grew to 9.823 billion rand on Thursday from 9.677 billion rand on Wednesday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
